title: reliability-experimentation-runway-slo-discovery-2026
summary: A pragmatic, cross-functional micro-sprint playbook for discovering, validating, and operationalizing SLOs tied to customer impact. Emphasizes short hypothesis-driven experiments, lightweight synthetic traffic harnesses, and a tight feedback loop with product and CS.
objectives:
- Rapidly identify 3 candidate SLOs for high-impact services in 6 weeks.
- Validate SLO signal fidelity and customer-impact mapping via experiments and telemetry.
- Produce an operational handbook and rollout checklist for each SLO to be used by service owners and product partners.
scope: Includes discovery and validation phases for 3 prioritized services: hosted-api-generation, batching-router, and embedding-indexer. Excludes infra procurement, long-term capacity planning, and deep model-level evaluation (those will be handled by dedicated follow-ups).
stakeholders:
- SRE: Morgan Hayes (lead), Riley Chen (metrics engineer)
- Product: Priya Narayanan (hosted API PM)
- Serving Runtime: Liam O'Connor
- Observability: Zara Malik
- Customer Success: Ana Gomez
- Security/Compliance on-call as needed
Notes: invite one engineer from each service team to the micro-sprint squad.
phases_and_timeline:
Week 0 (Kickoff): align on candidate services and hypothesis statements.
Weeks 1-2 (Discovery sprints): gather telemetry, sketch SLO targets, run lightweight customer-impact interviews.
Weeks 3-4 (Experimentation): run synthetic fault injections and traffic shaping to measure signal-quality and customer-impact proxies.
Week 5 (Analysis & Decision): select final SLO definitions, gate criteria, and rollout plan.
Week 6 (Handbook & Handoff): publish SLO handbooks, create rollout Jira epics, and schedule canary deployments.
Milestones: Discovery complete (end W2), Experiment results uploaded (end W4), Handbooks merged (end W6).
hypothesis_framework:
For each candidate SLO, define:
- Hypothesis: "If we target P99 latency < X ms for operation Y, then we will reduce customer query timeouts by Z% and lower support tickets by Q%"
- Signal: concrete metric(s) used to evaluate (latency percentiles, error rate, queue depth, tail-kv-cache-miss-rate)
- Customer proxy: support ticket triage tags, CS escalation frequency, demo recording dropouts
- Success criteria: measurable improvement in customer proxy OR clear operational behavior that maps to mitigation routes
Notes: keep hypotheses narrowly scoped and measurable.
experiment_design:
- Synthetic harness: small-scale traffic generator that replays production traces with parameterized tail behavior.
- Fault injection: network latency, throttled CPU, model worker restart, KV cache cold-starts.
- Measurement windows: baseline (48h), perturbation (6h), recovery (24h).
- Data collection: raw traces, APM spans, extracted percentiles, and CS ticket snapshots.
- Quick sanity checks: smoke assertion that perturbation changes the signal by >10% before deeper analysis.
Open questions: can we run perturbation on Dedicated without violating customer SLAs? If not, use canary region with synthetic tenants.
metrics_and_dashboards:
Minimum required metrics per SLO candidate:
- latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99 for key RPCs
- request_error_rate (total and per-error-class)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio and cold_start_rate (if applicable)
- queue_length and worker_utilization
- CS_ticket_rate with 'performance' label
Dashboards: create a compact 1-screen view (6 panels) per candidate with annotation layers for experiment windows. Owner: Zara Malik to create templates.
acceptance_criteria_and_gates:
To graduate an SLO from candidate -> operational: 
1) Signal stability: metric noise < 15% CV during baseline window.
2) Customer mapping: observed perturbation correlates to CS proxy in at least one experiment.
3) Runbook: mitigation steps and rollout plan documented and reviewed.
4) Observability: dashboards and alerts created with runbook links.
If any gate fails, plan a 2-week remediation sprint and re-run experiments.
communication_and_risk_plan:
- Weekly 30-min sync with stakeholders (Mon 10:00 PST).
- Rapid alerts: any experiment causing >2x baseline customer proxy triggers immediate rollback.
- Release note template for SLO rollouts that product will send to customers.
- Risk matrix: 
  * Risk: synthetic experiments accidentally hit production tenants -> Mitigation: run in canary with synthetic tenants, traffic tagging.
  * Risk: metric aggregation lag hides tail effects -> Mitigation: enable higher cardinality sampling and short retention stream for experiment windows.
- Escalation path: on-call SRE -> service lead -> product PM -> CS lead.
roles_and_responsibilities:
- SRE lead (Morgan): coordinate experiments, own decision to roll forward/stop.
- Metrics engineer (Riley): implement dashboards, ensure sampling, validate data quality.
- Product PM (Priya): own customer-impact framing, reach out to pilot customers for qualitative feedback.
- Runtime engineer (Liam): implement experiment hooks and safe-fail toggles.
- Observability (Zara): short-term data retention, alerting config.
- CS liaison (Ana): collect and summarize customer anecdotes during experiments.
kickoff_checklist:
- [ ] Confirm prioritized services and nominate engineering reps.
- [ ] Create experiment environment (canary/synthetic tenant).
- [ ] Create dashboards templates and link to this doc.
- [ ] Book weekly sync and set calendar invites.
- [ ] Open discovery Jira tickets (ENG-9312, ENG-9313, ENG-9314).
- [ ] Pre-approve rollback criteria with service leads.
Notes to self: start with the smallest surface area service to iterate on experiment tooling fast.
deliverables:
- 3 SLO candidate definitions with hypothesis blocks.
- Experiment artifacts: traffic scripts, fault injection configs, raw traces.
- Analysis report per service (short format: 1 page + graphs).
- Operational SLO handbook template and per-service handbooks.
- Jira epics for rollout and automation follow-ups.
retro_and_continuation: After week 6: run a 1-hour retro to capture what worked, what didn't, and immediate follow-ups. Expected continuation work: automated SLO guardrails, integration with Optimize recommendations, and a quarterly re-evaluation cadence for SLOs tied to new model versions.
parking_lot_and_open_questions:
- Do we want SLOs defined at model-variant level or at service-level with model-variant labels?
- What is the minimum viable alerting threshold that reduces noise for oncall?
- Can Dedicated customers opt out of certain SLO experiments? Need legal check.
- Who will own long-term trend evaluation (monthly regression detection)?
notes_to_self: Keep experiments visible and small. Aim for clear yes/no outcomes per hypothesis. If analysis is messy, favor more targeted instrumentation rather than broader experiments. Use customer quotes in the handbooks to make the impact tangible for execs and product.
conclusion: This runway is intentionally lightweight and hypothesis-driven to produce operationally useful SLOs quickly. The goal is not to be perfect on first pass but to create a repeatable, cross-functional pattern that scales across services.
